captions.linkedin:
We built Guardd with a simple goal: help families navigate the digital world together. We had our roadmap, packed with features we thought parents would need-filters, timers, the usual suspects. But then something happened in our beta group that changed everything.

Parents started asking us, quietly at first, if there was any way to see what their kids were searching for on YouTube. Not to block them, but just to understand. To have a window into their inner worlds.

So we built a small, almost hidden feature called Search Insights. It wasn’t flashy. It didn’t have a slick interface. It was just a simple list of search queries from a child’s device, stripped of all personal identifiers. And it turned out to be the feature nobody asked for, but everyone needed.

One mom told us she saw "how to tie shoes" searched twenty times one week. She realized her son was too embarrjerked to ask for help again. Another parent found searches for "why do I have two moms" and used it to start a beautiful conversation. These weren't moments of catching a kid doing something wrong. They were invitations to connect.

Today, Search Insights is Guardd’s most-used tool. It reminds us that digital safety isn't about control; it's about connection. It's less of a watchtower and more of a welcome mat for the conversations we hope to have.

What's one unexpected thing you've learned about your child this month?
